title: An agent's definition
description: An agent's definition. It holds the agent's model, instructions, tools and other settings. agent.definition returns a definition in the same format.

display_name.description: The name shown to people. Defaults to the agent's name.

description.description: What the agent is for, in words a person reads.

tools.description: The tools the agent can call. Each entry is one of these: the name of a built-in tool. files, for the file tools. server/*, for all tools of the MCP server named server. workers/*, for all tools from connected tool workers. self/*, for operations on the agent itself. agents/*, for operations on other agents. *, for all tools.

oneOf.description: The ID of the agent whose workspace is mounted.

shared.description: Other agents' workspaces to mount. Each key is the name of the mount, at shared/<name>/. Each value is an agent ID, or an agent ID and a mode. The resolver decides whether the agent can read or write. Set mode to read to mount a writable workspace as read-only.

workspace.description: Other agents' workspaces to mount. Only workspaces the resolver shares are mounted, and the agent's tools must include files.

context.description: Files to add to each turn. The files can come from the agent's workspace or a shared workspace. You can list up to 20 files. Their total size is limited to 16 KB. Set max_bytes to change the limit. The agent's tools must include files.

oneOf.description: The name of a policy the server has.
Policy rules, in the same format as a policy file.

timeout.description: The maximum length of a turn, in seconds.

idle_timeout.description: Seconds without work before the agent sleeps. It wakes on the next message or trigger. Defaults to the server's setting.

digest.description: Whether the agent writes a digest of each conversation to digests/ in its workspace before it sleeps. A later conversation finds it with search_files. It needs the files tool, and counts towards the agent's budget. Defaults to true.

max_iterations.description: The maximum number of tool-call rounds in one turn.

attempts.description: Retries for a failed model call. Defaults to 6. 0 disables retries.

max_wait.description: The maximum wait between retries, in seconds. Defaults to 60.

on_exhausted.description: What happens when all retries fail. ask asks a person whether to retry. fail fails the turn. Defaults to ask.

retries.description: How a turn retries a failed model call. Each retry waits a random delay of up to one second, doubling each time, or the provider's Retry-After, capped at max_wait. 4xx responses other than 408, 425 and 429 are not retried. The server's defaults apply if this is not set.

top_p.description: Top-p sampling. The model samples from the most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to this value.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens in one model response.

reasoning_effort.description: The reasoning effort for models that support it.

receive_timeout.description: Seconds a model call waits for a response. Defaults to 300.

stream_idle_timeout.description: Seconds a model's stream may be idle. Defaults to 300.

total_timeout.description: The maximum length of one model call, in seconds. Defaults to the turn's timeout.

model_options.description: Options for the agent's model calls. Only these keys are accepted. The server sets all other model options.

compaction.description: When the agent summarizes older history. The values are fractions of the model's context window. Set to false to turn off summarizing.

name.description: The trigger name. Defaults to trigger-1, trigger-2 and so on, by position in the list.

every.description: A cron expression, or an interval such as 30m.

timezone.description: The IANA time zone for a cron expression in every, such as Europe/Berlin. Defaults to Etc/UTC. Not used with an interval.

prompt.description: The prompt sent to the agent on each run.

prompt_file.description: Use instead of prompt. A file in the agent's workspace. Each run asks the agent to read the file and follow its instructions. The agent's tools must include files.

overlap.description: What happens if the agent is busy when the trigger fires. skip skips the run. queue runs it after the current turn. settle cancels a turn that is waiting for an approval and runs. If the turn isn't waiting for an approval, settle skips the run.

missed.description: What to do about runs missed while the server was down.

jitter.description: A random delay of up to this many seconds before each run.

feed.description: An RSS or Atom feed URL, or a list of them. The agent runs only when a feed has new entries, which are added below the prompt. The first check records the current entries without running the agent.

secret.description: The shared secret, as a reference, for example ${NAME}.

verify.description: How requests are verified. With shared, the request sends the secret as a bearer token or as the last path segment of the URL. With standard, the request is signed as the Standard Webhooks spec describes. Defaults to shared.

webhook.description: Use instead of every. An external service sends requests to the trigger. Each request runs the agent once.

triggers.description: Triggers that run the agent. Each trigger has a prompt or a prompt_file. Defining the agent again replaces all its triggers. To change one trigger, use PUT or DELETE /v1/agents/{key}/triggers/{trigger}. A scheduled trigger has every and an optional timezone. A feed trigger has feed. A webhook trigger has webhook, with its secret and verification method. It receives requests at POST /v1/hooks/{key}/{trigger}.

to.description: Notification targets defined by the resolver, or chat rooms such as slack:#updates.

on.description: The events that send a notification. The options are parked, failed and finished. Defaults to parked and failed.

notify.description: Where to send a notification when the agent parks, fails or finishes. Use a target that the resolver defines, or a chat room like slack:#updates. You can also give a list of targets, or an object with to and on. Chat rooms are in the workspace that the resolver sets for the channel.

channels.description: Names of the chat channels the agent can reply in.
